meta.role: design spec written by the history + design study; the build is judged against this file and SENBON_DESIGN_SHEET.png
meta.sheet_script: WorkFiles/senbon/senbon_design_sheet.py (Blender 5.2 headless; rebuilds the sheet and the 'derived' block from this file)
meta.units: millimetres unless a key says otherwise; Blender builds in metres (1 BU = 1 m), so divide by 1000
meta.status_flags: DESIGN = our own choice for this set (no single source); SOURCED = the number follows a source in the study; PACK = copied from the existing shuriken pack so the needles match it
meta.ip: Original design. Generic historical form (round throwing needle, hari-gata). No anime design, name or symbol; the word 'senbon' is a generic Japanese term. Do not use Wikimedia Commons 'Senbon.svg' (fan art) as a reference.

pack_conventions.orientation: long axis = object X, +X toward the (front) point; Z up; built at real scale, transforms applied
pack_conventions.pivot: centre of mass by volume of the finished LOD0 steel (Needle: the geometric centre by symmetry; Heavy: computed, see derived)

cross_section_segments.note: the plan's 12 / 8 / 6; the swell and the facets are carried by the profile stations, not by more sides

pack_conventions.collision: one convex hull UCX_<base>_LOD0_00, <= 24 vertices, LOD0 0.0 mm outside it
pack_conventions.sockets: Empties SOCKET_<base>_LOD0_<Name> + .sockets.json sidecar (ue_import_sockets.py); socket X axis = the needle's +X
pack_conventions.screen_size_rule: the shuriken pack's switch distances (LOD1 at about 0.89 m, LOD2 at about 2.54 m) scaled by bounds radius R: S1 = 1.778 R / 0.89 m, S2 = 1.778 R / 2.54 m (the spike ships 0.1501 / 0.0525 at R 75 mm)
pack_conventions.texture_rule: power-of-two, full mips, BC sRGB / ORM linear / N DirectX, baked AO in ORM.R; non-square maps allowed as on the spike (2048 x 512)
pack_conventions.materials: pack masters only: steel slots -> M_Steel_Master instances MI_Senbon_<Item>_Steel; the Heavy's wrap -> M_Fabric_Master instance MI_Senbon_Heavy_Wrap (recolourable, as the kunai grip)
pack_conventions.ownership: ADVISORY block. WorkFiles/senbon/SENBON_BUILD_PLAN.md (the game + tech study, written in parallel) owns the frame, sockets (Grip / Tip / Trail / Throw / Embed), collision, triangle budgets, LOD sides and screen sizes, maps and the projectile conventions; where it differs from this block, the plan wins. THIS file owns the design: the item count, every profile dimension, the point and tail forms, the wrap and the finish.

steel_coat.description: blackened (oxide) steel, the pack's coat: very dark, faintly violet, satin; fine scratches and a few dark specks; NO hammer texture (drawn wire, not forged plate)

ground_point.description: bright ground steel on every point surface (Needle: both cones; Heavy: the three facets), with fine grind lines running ALONG the axis; the coat ends at the grind line with a 1.5-2.5 mm worn fade back onto the body (not a painted stripe)

body_wear.description: faint polished wear lines along the body where fingers slide on release (Needle: |x| 0-25 mm; Heavy: just ahead of the wrap, s 54-80 mm); value lift at most +25 % of the coat; no bright stripes

wrap.description: Heavy only: twisted cotton thread, close-wound single layer, matte; end bindings slightly tighter and raised; no lacquer gloss, no tassel
wrap.thread_relief: normal map + BC/ORM detail; the wrap's outer shell and the two bindings are real geometry
wrap.status: PACK colour (the kunai grip MI_Kunai_Plain_Wrap ships #373532); wrap form DESIGN after the Negishi tail binding (cotton string) without the hair tassel

SM_Senbon_Needle.title: Senbon, standard needle (double-pointed volley needle)
SM_Senbon_Needle.role: game: the volley needle (3 thrown at once, fanned, direct no-spin throw); Fab: the archetypal senbon
SM_Senbon_Needle.symmetry: mirror-symmetric about x = 0 and round (C-infinity about X); both ends identical
SM_Senbon_Needle.frame: x measured from the centre, mm; +X = the 'front' point (identical to the back one)

profile.body_law: D(x) = 2.30 + 0.50 * (1 - (x / 50)^2) for |x| <= 50 (a smooth parabolic swell, thickest at the centre, no crease at x = 0)
profile.point: straight cone from the shoulder ring to the tip on each end
profile.grind_line: the shoulder ring at |x| = 50 is a HARD edge (profile angle changes 0.57 deg -> 4.38 deg, a 3.8 deg crease) and the coat / bright-steel boundary
profile.status: DESIGN; length and 'thickest at the centre, two points' follow the study sections 2 and 4 (hair-needle scale, senbon maker's balance rule); diameter set by the visibility floor in study section 5

Grip.note: centre / balance point: the double-pointed needle is held across the fingers at its middle (study section 4); this is the one place the needle differs from the plan's 40 mm-from-butt rule, which assumes a single-pointed needle

Tip.note: front tip: stick-in decal, impact FX

Trail.note: back tip: ribbon / trail emitter (the needle is sub-pixel past ~3 m; the trail carries the read)

Embed.rule: the plan's rule: Tip minus the default embed depth

budgets_tris.note: plan section 5; the parabolic swell needs about 6 stations per half at LOD0, 2 at LOD1, none at LOD2

SM_Senbon_Needle.lod_notes: LOD1: 8 sides, body swell 3 rings per half; LOD2: 6 sides, shoulder rings + tips only (the swell may go)

texture.note: one long strip (130 mm x 8.8 mm circumference) + the two cones; 2048 x 256 holds it at ~14 px/mm; justify any change in the report

SM_Senbon_Needle.throw: jiki-daho (direct, no spin); volley of 3, fanned +-4 deg
SM_Senbon_Needle.differs_from_spike: round not square; 2.8 mm not 6 mm; double-pointed and mirror-symmetric (spike: one point, short tail taper); thickest at the centre with a visible swell; ~1/9 of the spike's mass; 130 mm not 150 mm

SM_Senbon_Heavy.title: Senbon, heavy needle (single point, three-facet tip, thread-wrapped tail)
SM_Senbon_Heavy.role: game: the heavy single throw (slower, more damage, front-weighted so it flies point-first); Fab: variety piece with a recolourable wrap
SM_Senbon_Heavy.cross_section: round steel; three ground facets at the point; round wrap shell at the tail
SM_Senbon_Heavy.frame: s measured from the butt face (s = 0) toward the tip (s = 170), mm; the object origin is moved to the centre of mass afterwards (derived.SM_Senbon_Heavy.com_from_butt_mm)

tail_steel.note: constant; bare and visible over s 0-6, covered by the wrap over s 6-54

rear_binding.edges: crisp 0.15 mm round on both outer corners

wrap.note: single layer of 0.6 mm thread over the Ø 2.8 steel = Ø 4.0; drawn and built at Ø 4.2 (0.1 mm of thread flattening / glue allowance each side)

front_binding.edges: crisp 0.15 mm round on both outer corners

body.law: linear taper, thickest at the front (front-weighted, the Negishi principle, without the octagonal head); chosen so the centre of mass sits about 9 mm ahead of the middle (see derived)

point.form: trihedral: three flat ground facets meeting at the tip, cut into the round Ø 4.5 stock
point.azimuth_convention: angle in the YZ plane from +Y toward +Z (90 = +Z, facing up)
point.facet_rule: each facet plane contains the tip (s = 170 on the axis) and lies 2.25 mm from the axis at s = 148 along its own normal: distance from axis h(s) = (170 - s) * 2.25 / 22
point.grind_line: each facet meets the round stock along an elliptical arc: at the facet's centreline it starts at s = 148, between facets (azimuths 30, 150, 270) the round land runs on to s = 159 (= 170 - 22/2, independent of the diameter); hard edges
point.ridges: three straight facet-facet ridges from s = 159 to the tip at azimuths 30, 150, 270; ridge radius r(s) = (170 - s) * 4.5 / 22
point.status: DESIGN; three-facet point after the study's note on the Shirai-ryu needle's 'triangular point' (single retailer, see study)

profile.status: DESIGN; length and Ø within the sourced hari-gata ranges (study section 2)

Grip.note: wrap centre, s = 30 (40 mm from the butt in the plan's rule falls on the wrap too; use 30, the wrap's middle)

Embed.rule: the plan's rule: Tip minus the default embed depth

budgets_tris.note: the plan's 1,000 cap for a tail feature: the wrap shell + two bindings and the three facets; LOD2 merges wrap and bindings into one step and the facets into a cone

SM_Senbon_Heavy.lod_notes: LOD1: 8 sides, facets kept as 3 planes, bindings as single steps; LOD2: 6 sides, wrap and bindings merged into one cylinder, facets as one cone

wrap.note: the wrap needs about 3 px per 0.6 mm thread turn to read; plus the recolour detail map(s) the Fabric master requires, made by the pack's own tooling

SM_Senbon_Heavy.differs_from_spike: round not square; three-facet point not a four-facet pyramid; thread-wrapped tail with bindings (the spike is bare steel); thickens toward the point (Ø 2.8 -> 4.5, centre of mass ahead of the middle) where the spike is a uniform 6 mm bar; 170 mm / ~12 g against 150 mm / 37 g

not_in_this_set.bundle: not a mesh: a volley is 3 SM_Senbon_Needle instances placed by the game
not_in_this_set.holder_case: deferred (study section 6): a belt tube case earns a place only once the character has a belt socket; it needs a wood / lacquer look the pack masters do not have
not_in_this_set.tassel: no tassel or hair tail on either needle (that is the shuriken pack's planned Negishi dart)
not_in_this_set.marks: no stamped characters, crests or maker's marks

SM_Shuriken_Spike.source: WorkFiles/shuriken/spike_report.json build_to (frozen; shown on the sheet for contrast only)

acceptance.silhouette: side and top silhouettes of LOD0 within 0.05 mm of the profile in this file at every 1 mm station (measured on the mesh, not the render)
acceptance.diameters: Needle: D(0) 2.80 +- 0.02, D(+-50) 2.30 +- 0.02, tips at +-65.0 +- 0.1; Heavy: wrap 4.20 +- 0.03, bindings 4.60 +- 0.03, steel 2.80 over s 0-54 and 4.50 at s 148 +- 0.02, ridges start at s 159 +- 0.3, tip at s 170.0 +- 0.1, centre of mass within 1 mm of derived.com_from_butt_mm
acceptance.mass: steel volume x 7.85 g/cm3 within +-3 % of derived.mass_g (cotton wrap 0.6 g/cm3 counted separately)
acceptance.look: side-by-side with the sheet's views: round reads round, the swell reads, the Heavy's three facets and their elliptical grind lines read at the 5:1 detail scale; bright points against the blackened body
